text:
Jordan: quick help — we're seeing missing spans from the workermgr async worker for a few job runs. I can't find related traces in the Observability console for run id job-20260316-2210. Any quick checklist where to look (logs/metrics/traces)? Could sampling be the culprit?

Anya: start with the traces dashboard and the service map. link: https://console.redwood.ai/observability/dashboards/service-map?svc=workermgr — if you don't see the service there it usually means traces aren't being exported or the resource attr is wrong. Also check logs -> ingestion errors.

Sam: if sampling hides them you'd still see a handful of traces unless sampler prob is ~0. Check env: OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER and OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG. In our docker-compose for workermgr it's at ops/workermgr/.env. Example we use:```
OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=parentbased_traceidratio
OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG=0.02
```
Lowering to 0.1 for debug helped us last time.

oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Alert fired: workermgr_high_error_rate (count 37) — see runbook: https://console.redwood.ai/runbooks/workermgr-errors

Leo: another common issue — the async prefetcher spawns a subprocess that doesn't get the tracer provider injected. If spans are null you'll see logs like:```
ERROR workermgr.fetcher: span_id=null trace_id=0x9f3a7d... context=missing
```
Fix is to explicitly propagate ctx when you spawn threads/processes, e.g. for multiprocessing:```
from opentelemetry import trace, propagate
ctx = propagate.extract({})
# pass ctx into child and call propagate.inject when sending network requests
```
Or use our helper wrapper: ops/python/tracing/wrap_subprocess.py (small utility that initializes SDK from env).

Marta: Jordan — can you paste the service resource attrs from the agent logs? Also I'll open a tiny PR to add the subprocess wrapper to workermgr once we confirm. Ping me for CR.

Jordan: pasted logs snippet:```
2026-03-16T22:10:12Z workermgr[pid:2345] ERROR fetch_task failed span=null trace_id=null error="kvcache timeout"
2026-03-16T22:10:12Z workermgr[pid:2345] INFO starting prefetcher pid=2350
```
Looks like trace ids are null. Where's that helper wrapper?

Anya: wrapper path: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/blob/main/python/tracing/wrap_subprocess.py — it's a tiny file that calls tracerprovider on child startup. We should also check the instrumentations: make sure celery/kafka instrumentation versions are pinned to our supported list (see obs/compat matrix).

Sam: quick repro tip — run a local docker image with OTEL_LOG_LEVEL=debug and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT pointing at staging-otel:4317 and trigger a job. You should see Exporter/Span logs if SDK is actually capturing.

Marta: I'll open PR to add the wrapper + test that child processes report spans to staging. @Jordan add me to the issue and I'll grab a review from @Leo.

Jordan: thanks all — also can someone tune the alert sensitivity? that workermgr error alert is noisy for short bursts. If we can't root cause quickly maybe raise threshold or increase evaluation window.

Leo: agreed. I'll propose new thresholds: increase count window to 10m and change severity to P3 for now. Filing an alert PR in observability repo.

Anya: added dashboard links for traces/metrics/logs in the issue so next oncall can find them quickly. https://console.redwood.ai/observability/dashboards/workermgr-full-view

oncall-bot: Note: incident slack channel created #incident-workermgr-182572 — join if you're investigating.

Jordan: perfect, I'll follow up with logs from staging run and assign the issue. Thanks :thumbsup:
